0x80070005.title: Access Denied / Permission Error
0x80070005.description: Access denied - permission issue on WinSxS or SoftwareDistribution directories preventing installation of updates.
manual_steps: Open an elevated Command Prompt (Run as Administrator).
Take ownership of SoftwareDistribution: takeown /f C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution /r /d y
Reset Access Control Lists (ACLs): icacls C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution /reset /t /c /l /q
Reset WinSxS permissions using SubInACL or default TrustedInstaller ACLs.
Restart the Windows Update service: net start wuauserv

0x8024402c.title: Update Server Unreachable / Proxy Misconfiguration
0x8024402c.description: Proxy or firewall misconfiguration or corrupted update cache files preventing connection to Windows Update servers.
manual_steps: Open an elevated Command Prompt.
Reset the WinHTTP proxy settings: netsh winhttp reset proxy
Clear temporary Internet and update files: del /q /s %temp%\*
Flush the DNS resolver cache: ipconfig /flushdns
Check Windows Firewall rules for Windows Update endpoints.

0x8024402f.title: Update Installation Loop Failure
0x8024402f.description: Windows Update installation repeatedly fails due to corrupted datastore or broken catalog databases.
manual_steps: Stop core services: net stop wuauserv & net stop cryptSvc & net stop bits & net stop msiserver
Rename C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution to SoftwareDistribution.old
Rename C:\Windows\System32\catroot2 to catroot2.old
Restart services: net start wuauserv & net start cryptSvc & net start bits & net start msiserver
Retry Windows Update from Settings or Control Panel.

0x80072EFD.title: Update Server Connection Interrupted
0x80072EFD.description: Cannot connect to Windows Update server due to network timeout, TLS cipher mismatch, or security proxy blockage.
manual_steps: Verify Internet connectivity by reaching public endpoints.
Ensure TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 are enabled in Internet Options (inetcpl.cpl).
Reset WinHTTP proxy configuration: netsh winhttp reset proxy
Add update URLs (update.microsoft.com, windowsupdate.com) to trusted firewall zones.
Restart BITS and Windows Update services.

0xC1900101.title: Windows 10/11 Upgrade Rollback / Driver Conflict
0xC1900101.description: Upgrade rollback caused by third-party filter drivers, disk corruption, or incompatible hardware drivers.
manual_steps: Disconnect all non-essential external peripherals (USB drives, dongles, secondary webcams).
Run System File Checker: sfc /scannow
Execute Component Store repair: DISM.exe /Online /Cleanup-image /Restorehealth
Clean staging drivers and update graphics / chipset drivers from vendor.
Perform clean boot before initiating feature upgrade.

0xC1900210.title: Upgrade Compatibility Scan Complete (No Blockers)
0xC1900210.description: MOSETUP_E_COMPAT_SCANONLY_NO_ISSUES: Compatibility scan succeeded with no actionable blocking issues detected.
manual_steps: Verify Windows Setup media integrity.
Check setup logs in C:\$WINDOWS.~BT\Sources\Panther for silent process terminations.
Retry upgrade with clean boot.

0xC1900208.title: Incompatible Application Blocking Upgrade
0xC1900208.description: MOSETUP_E_COMPAT_APPS_BLOCK: Incompatible software, security tool, or legacy utility blocking the Windows 10/11 upgrade.
manual_steps: Review incompatible application list in Windows Setup or Panther logs.
Uninstall conflicting legacy apps (e.g. outdated virtual drives, third-party firewalls, obsolete utility tools).
Reboot and restart upgrade setup.

0xC1900204.title: Selected Edition Not Eligible for Upgrade
0xC1900204.description: MOSETUP_E_COMPAT_MIG_CHOICE_NO_DEFAULT: Selected Windows edition or architecture does not support direct in-place migration.
manual_steps: Ensure installation media matches current OS architecture (x64 to x64, not x86).
Verify Windows Edition upgrade path (e.g., Home to Pro, not Enterprise to Home).
Use official Media Creation Tool to generate matching edition ISO.

0xC1900200.title: System Hardware Requirements Not Met
0xC1900200.description: MOSETUP_E_COMPAT_SYSREQ_NOT_MET: Machine does not meet minimum hardware requirements (TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, RAM, or supported CPU).
manual_steps: Check TPM 2.0 status in tpm.msc and enable in UEFI BIOS if available.
Verify Secure Boot is enabled in BIOS/UEFI.
Ensure at least 4GB RAM and 64GB storage available.
Run PC Health Check app from Microsoft.

0xC190020E.title: Insufficient Disk Space for Upgrade
0xC190020E.description: MOSETUP_E_COMPAT_DISKSPACE_BLOCK: System partition has insufficient free space to unpack and stage upgrade files.
manual_steps: Free at least 20-30GB of space on primary drive C:.
Run WindowsFixKit Storage Cleanup (Option 4).
Attach an external USB drive with 32GB+ free to provide staging storage during setup.

0x800f0922.title: SSU / .NET / System Partition Space Failure
0x800f0922.description: Servicing Stack Update or .NET installation failed due to insufficient System Reserved / EFI partition space or active VPN blocking update callbacks.
manual_steps: Disconnect all active VPN connections and third-party security firewalls.
Verify that System Reserved or EFI System Partition (ESP) has at least 50MB free space.
Enable or repair .NET Framework 3.5 and 4.x via DISM /Online /Enable-Feature.
Clear corrupted CBS servicing logs under C:\Windows\Logs\CBS.
Re-run Windows Update.

windows_update_stuck_zero_percent.title: Windows Update Stuck at 0% / Checking for Updates Hang
windows_update_stuck_zero_percent.description: Update download stuck at 0% or hangs at Checking for updates screen
manual_steps: Check disk space (need 15GB+ free)
Temporarily disable third-party antivirus
Verify internet connection
Restart and retry

third_party_install_badimageformat.title: .NET BadImageFormatException / PresentationFramework Crash
third_party_install_badimageformat.description: App installer fails with System.BadImageFormatException referencing PresentationFramework or similar .NET assembly - usually a corrupt or missing .NET Framework installation
manual_steps: Run .NET Framework Repair Tool from Microsoft
Reinstall .NET Framework 4.x
Check Windows Update for optional .NET updates
Retry installer as administrator

wifi_missing_post_update.title: Wi-Fi Adapter Missing Post-Update
wifi_missing_post_update.description: Wi-Fi adapter or tray icon disappears after a Windows update or driver migration failure.
manual_steps: Open Device Manager (devmgmt.msc).
Under Network Adapters, look for disabled or hidden wireless devices.
Right-click the Wi-Fi adapter and select Enable device.
Restart WLAN AutoConfig service: net start WlanSvc
Scan for hardware changes via Action -> Scan for hardware changes.

bluetooth_missing_post_update.title: Bluetooth Icon & Service Missing Post-Update
bluetooth_missing_post_update.description: Bluetooth icon, device settings, or core Bluetooth support service disappears after a Windows update.
manual_steps: Open Services console (services.msc).
Locate Bluetooth Support Service (bthserv), set Startup type to Automatic, and Start the service.
Locate Bluetooth Audio Gateway Service (BTAGService) and start it.
In Device Manager, check Bluetooth radios and reinstall default Microsoft Bluetooth driver if needed.

network_no_internet.title: Network Adapter Connected Without Internet
network_no_internet.description: Network adapter is connected to local router/switch but cannot route packets or obtain public internet access.
manual_steps: Reset Winsock catalog: netsh winsock reset
Reset TCP/IP stack: netsh int ip reset
Release and renew DHCP IP addresses: ipconfig /release followed by ipconfig /renew
Flush and register DNS entries: ipconfig /flushdns && ipconfig /registerdns
Restart computer to apply socket resets.

dns_not_resolving.title: DNS Lookups Failing / Websites Unreachable
dns_not_resolving.description: Domain name resolution fails across browsers and applications while IP-level connectivity remains active.
manual_steps: Flush DNS resolver cache: ipconfig /flushdns
Restart DNS Client service if accessible: net stop dnscache && net start dnscache
Configure static or fallback DNS servers (Primary: 1.1.1.1, Secondary: 8.8.8.8) on active adapters.
Verify resolution using: nslookup google.com

hdd_ssd_unhealthy.title: Physical Storage Degradation / SMART Failure
hdd_ssd_unhealthy.description: Physical disk SMART counters report excessive wear (>80%), bad sectors, or uncorrected read error spikes.
manual_steps: Immediately backup critical files to external drive or cloud storage.
Run chkdsk scan: chkdsk C: /scan
Optimize and re-trim SSD volumes: Optimize-Volume -DriveLetter C -ReTrim
Check OEM disk management software (Samsung Magician, Crucial Executive, WD Dashboard) for firmware updates.

ram_error_detected.title: RAM Exhaustion / Memory Pool Depletion
ram_error_detected.description: Available physical memory is below 10% or system memory caches are overloaded with non-paged pool leaks.
manual_steps: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic: mdsched.exe
Close memory-intensive background apps or browser instances.
Inspect Task Manager -> Performance -> Memory -> Non-paged pool.
Ensure virtual memory / paging file size is set to system managed.

battery_degraded.title: Battery Capacity Degradation (<60%)
battery_degraded.description: Battery full charge capacity has degraded significantly below 60% of original factory design capacity.
manual_steps: Generate detailed battery report: powercfg /batteryreport
Enable Battery Saver threshold at 20% in Windows Settings.
Lower screen brightness and configure display sleep timeouts to 5 minutes.
Calibrate battery by charging to 100% and discharging, or replace aged battery pack.

cpu_overheating.title: CPU Overheating / Thermal Throttling
cpu_overheating.description: CPU thermal sensors report elevated core temperatures exceeding 80°C under standard loads.
manual_steps: Inspect laptop vents or desktop heatsink fans for dust accumulation.
Configure power plan Processor Maximum State to 99% to prevent aggressive thermal boosting.
Ensure active system cooling policy is enabled.
Reapply high-conductivity thermal paste if hardware is older than 2-3 years.

storage_almost_full.title: Disk Partition Space Critical (>90% Full)
storage_almost_full.description: Primary or system drive partition is above 90% capacity, risking update failures and filesystem fragmentation.
manual_steps: Empty the Recycle Bin.
Run Windows Disk Cleanup: cleanmgr /autoclean /d C
Purge temporary folders (%temp% and C:\Windows\Temp).
Clear Delivery Optimization cache in Settings -> System -> Storage.

startup_bloat.title: Excessive Startup Programs (>15 Entries)
startup_bloat.description: High number of startup applications and autostart launchers slowing down Windows boot and consuming idle RAM.
manual_steps: Open Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc) and go to the 'Startup apps' tab.
Right-click and disable non-essential high-impact launchers (Steam, Discord, Spotify, Updaters).
Clean broken startup registry entries in HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run.
Use msconfig or Autoruns for advanced autostart service auditing.
